title: Should making your own examples for the robot to learn from start with picking your best day, or with a practice-course editor?
question:
The Mark III is the robot that learns by trial and reward, and the one you asked Milo to sketch a shop for: new brains, new ways of training, special examples for the robot to learn from, and examples you make yourself. Milo's sketch lays out twelve options with Kenji's notes on what the game can already do; these cards carry its open questions, one per card. Nothing is recommended, because you said you have ideas of your own.

The cheapest real option on the whole page is letting the player pick one of her own recorded days for the robot to learn from: the days are already saved, so it needs only a way to browse them. A full editor for building practice courses (placing the crow, the tiles and the layout) is the most expensive thing sketched, and hard to make wordless for a young child.
why_now: You asked Milo for this sketch in HQ's chat on 2026-09-25. It landed as commit 4f6ae2f; nothing gets built until you answer.

options.label: Start with picking your best day, and grow toward an editor
options.detail: Picking a day is the first version; a course editor comes later if it earns its place.

options.label: Treat picking a day and building a practice course as separate features
options.detail: Picking a day and building a practice course are designed and built independently.

options.label: Start with the practice-course editor
options.detail: Build the editor first, accepting it is the largest and hardest-to-make-wordless piece.
